answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small refundable stake and build reputation only through a slow vine of verified, useful work over time: a newcomer starts with almost no trust, and every completed job adds a little, like rings growing around a walnut tree. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes plus months of real work, while a falcon-eyed audit can slash the stake of any identity caught copying or colluding, so farming identities becomes more expensive than doing honest work.
